Theorem part (c) is proved, per the proposal's own attack sketch step (3), by the termwise sandwich 0 <= C_X(h) <= C_s S(h) X against the absolute envelope of the resonant kernel. Any chain consuming only that sandwich must survive the sieve-consistent adversary C*(h) = C_s S(h) X on the kernel's positive-sign set; since the height window avoids tau = 0, psi(0) = 0, the kernel is mean-zero with positive-part mass bounded below (a nonnegative mean-zero kernel would be identically zero), so the envelope evaluates to ~ C_s X = C_s T^{1+eta}, not the claimed eta^2 T log^3 T. I re-derived the scaling independently (partial summation: int_T^X (L - log t) dt ~ X against main T L^3/6pi) and reproduced the killer's 'deceptive dip' numerically (env/main = 0.057 at T = 4000, 0.014 at 10^6, minimum ~0.004 near 10^12, divergent thereafter) — the toy numerics and the entire M0 program live where the divergent term is invisible, so the designed kill-switch cannot fire (killer finding 3 follows). Under the adjudication standards this is both 'claimed proportion gain impossible from stated inputs' and 'first theorem is a known-hard problem in disguise', which refutes even a proportion-scoped Track A direction.
